header:
Date: 2027-02-08
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Mills (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Evan Ortiz (Redwood Solutions), Maya Chen (AmberLight Head of Cloud Networking), Roberto Diaz (AmberLight Security Architect), Sana Qureshi (AmberLight Platform), Tom Adler (AmberLight CISO joined 00:38)
Recording: auto
Meeting type: Discovery - Private/VPC deployment intake
summary: AmberLight is evaluating Redwood Private with VPC-only connectivity. Primary concerns: strict egress rules, cross-account VPC peering vs PrivateLink, regional model availability, and HSM/KMS integration. They want a pilot with low-latency routing from their EU and US prod VPCs and auditability for SOC2 and finance-regulated data. Next steps: share diagrams, Terraform snippets, SOC2 docs, and schedule a 2hr pilot kickoff to align network owners.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Mills: hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to walk through how Redwood Private would plug into AmberLight's VPCs, understand constraints. i know we have a couple of folks from networking and security so 
[00:18] Maya Chen: yeah thanks Jordan, happy to be here. quick ask up front — all production traffic must not traverse public internet, and we need egress filtering per subnet. basically private-only.
[00:33] Priya Shah: great, that's a common pattern. we support private endpoints and vpc peering patterns, plus transit-gw attachements. one Q: do you prefer privatelink-style endpoints or peering? both have tradeoffs.
[00:48] Roberto Diaz: we lean to privatelink for tighter control and to avoid CIDR collisions but we also have strict egress proxies in place that need static IPs, so we need to map the path end-to-end.
[01:05] Evan Ortiz: just to add, Redwood Private can be deployed either as a customer-managed private control plane in your VPC or as a managed private tenancy where we bring a dedicated pool into your VPC with privatelink. terminology sometimes gets messy in notes — folks call it private link, private endpoints, columnlink — all the same thing here.
[01:30] Sana Qureshi: can you explain the difference operationally? like, who manages NAT and route tables?
[01:38] Priya Shah: sure, with a PrivateLink approach you create NLBs in our account and we give you the endpoint service name, you create an interface endpoint in your VPC; your team keeps control of route tables and security groups. with peering, you need non-overlapping CIDRs and transit-gw in some cases. peering is simpler for high throughput but more coupling.
[02:05] Maya Chen: we use transit-gw for most centralised services, but our security folks prefer endpoint services for audit boundaries. also curious about cross-region: we have eu-west-1 primary and us-east-1 DR. do we need separate endpoints per region?
[02:23] Jordan Mills: yes, region limitations exist. models and private endpoints are region-scoped; we can replicate model variants into multiple regions but that adds sync and cost. typically customers create endpoints in each region where traffic originates.
[02:40] Tom Adler: sorry jumped on late — agree with region separation, also need to confirm data residency. anything stored for logs or caching — is that in our VPC?
[02:50] Priya Shah: good question. KV cache and ephemeral traces are kept in the Redwood runtime, but for Private we can configure retention and routing to ship audit logs into your S3 / ELK via VPC egress. we also support customer-side KMS for encryption keys — we integrate with AWS KMS external keys, and HSM connectors on-prem if needed. note: sometimes documentation says KV cash which is a bad auto transcript so just clarifying.
[03:20] Roberto Diaz: KMS integration is critical. we require CMEK for any model artifacts or logs that are customer-sensitive. do you support BYOK with HSM-backed keys?
[03:30] Priya Shah: yes, we support customer-managed keys and HSM integration for Private deployments. we can show the KMS flow and key access policies in the pilot docs.
[03:43] Jordan Mills: can i ask about your current CIDR layout? any RFC1918 reuse?
[03:49] Maya Chen: we have 10.0.0.0/8 backbone but split across 100+ accounts. transit-gw handles most, however our payments VPC is 10.200.0.0/16 isolated for compliance.
[04:03] Evan Ortiz: that could be a blocker for peering. for peering you need non-overlap so PrivateLink likely. also about egress — do you have forced NATs or static egress IPs?
[04:14] Roberto Diaz: yes static egress via NAT instances and a proxy fleet, we record outbound destinations for audit. we would need Redwood to allow egress through our proxies or present fixed IPs for outbound to allow firewall rules.
[04:29] Priya Shah: two approaches: 1) route outbound tokens through your proxy via the endpoint's subnet rules, or 2) we host egress NAT in the same region as the private endpoints and provide static IPs (this is more of a dedicated option and would require a small egress pool). both are doable, tradeoffs on cost and control.
[04:55] Maya Chen: what's latency like if we go dedicated egress in-region? our SLAs for inference are 100ms p95 target.
[05:05] Jordan Mills: our Dedicated pools can meet that if colocated in the same AZ and with proper routing — but if you proxy through additional hops or cross-region calls that will add latency. we can run benchmarks with a sample prompt from your app during the pilot.
[05:25] Sana Qureshi: how do you handle failover? if a region is down will calls route to another region? we have strict compliance that says no cross-border data movement without approval.
[05:35] Priya Shah: we have routing policies: failover can happen, but for compliance we can restrict routing by policy to not cross region boundaries. for instance, EU traffic stays in eu-west-1. automatic fallback is optional; we wouldn't enable cross-border by default.
[05:56] Roberto Diaz: i want to understand audit logs — can we push all access logs into our S3 with encryption and lifecycle?
[06:05] Evan Ortiz: yes we support streaming logs to customer S3 buckets via VPC endpoints and we can include detailed per-request metadata. retention and masking rules are configurable; we can redact prompts in flight for privacy.
[06:23] Maya Chen: about networking: do we need to open ports? security teams hate extra surface area.
[06:30] Priya Shah: only TLS over private endpoints; interface endpoints use ENIs and security groups you control. no broad internet ports required.
[06:42] Maya Chen: excellent. can you summarize recommended topology for us?
[06:47] Jordan Mills: recommended is interface endpoint per region, using our endpoint service. place the endpoint in a private subnet with a security group that allows your application subnets. route 10.x traffic to the endpoint. for high throughput you can add multiple AZs. if you need ultra-low-latency and predictable throughput, consider Redwood Dedicated with an in-vpc deployment model — that gives you dedicated GPU capacity accessible via the same endpoint pattern.
[07:18] Sana Qureshi: any concerns about egress bandwidth limits for big batched embedding jobs? we're planning nightly bulk embeddings of historical logs.
[07:28] Priya Shah: bulk jobs are frequently run via a dedicated job queue. for embeddings we recommend running them during off-peak windows and using batching. Dedicated pools have higher sustained throughput and can be sized for your batch window.
[07:46] Tom Adler: security question — SSO, RBAC? we need SAML and SCIM provisioning and audit trails.
[07:55] Jordan Mills: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning, RBAC with token scoping, and audit logs. in Private we can tie into your identity provider and limit token issuance to specified roles.
[08:10] Roberto Diaz: liability question — for PII and payment data we need a contract clause restricting model training and retention. what does Redwood do regarding fine-tuning and retention?
[08:22] Priya Shah: by default we don't train customer data, and for Private deployment we can disable any persistent training or telemetry. we'll include contract language via legal; Jordan will loop in enterprise legal.
[08:35] Maya Chen: ok on practicalities, can you share an example terraform snippet for creating the interface endpoint and the route table association?
[08:45] Priya Shah: yes, i'll put together a starter terraform module showing the aws_vpc_endpoint for com.redwood.private-service, security groups, and route table examples.
[08:56] Evan Ortiz: tiny gotcha: sometimes our docs call the service name redwood-private-service and sometimes redwood-private. i'll make sure the snippet uses the canonical service name for your region.
[09:08] Maya Chen: naming consistency helps. also how does version pinning of models work for private? we need to guarantee the same model across environments for reproducible outputs.
[09:18] Jordan Mills: customers can pin model versions per route. Redwood Console exposes rollouts and can do canary traffic splits. for Private you can pin to a specific build and disable auto-updates.
[09:32] Sana Qureshi: what about tokenization and cost visibility? finance wants per-route token breakdowns.
[09:40] Priya Shah: Console provides token-level cost reporting per model/route and per-token breakdowns over time. you can export to your billing system or integrate with our API.
[09:53] Roberto Diaz: one more on encryption in transit — we need mutual TLS for endpoint auth. do you support mTLS to the private endpoints?
[10:02] Priya Shah: interface endpoints terminate TLS on your side, but we can support mTLS between your app and the endpoint via client certs if you want. for service-to-service we use TLS and token auth.
[10:18] Jordan Mills: i want to chart a pilot: we propose a 2-week pilot — week 1 network setup and security review, week 2 workload validation and latency/cost benchmarks. does that timeline look reasonable?
[10:31] Maya Chen: yes, with the caveat our security review has to sign off first. the pilot can't touch production data until white-listing is done.
[10:41] Tom Adler: add me to the security review thread; i'll give a pre-approval list.
[10:45] Jordan Mills: great, we'll include a security checklist.
[10:48] [00:11:32] Priya Shah: (screen share) i pulled a rough diagram — left is AmberLight VPCs (payments, api, analytics), middle is transit-gw, right is Redwood Private endpoints per region. arrows show interface endpoints from each VPC to the Redwood endpoint service.
[11:00] Maya Chen: that matches our mental model. do you support route propagation to route tables? we rely on propagated routes from transit-gw to avoid manual updates.
[11:12] Priya Shah: yes transit-gw works; interface endpoints don't create propagated routes but you can use route table associations depending on traffic flow. we'll show both patterns in the terraform example.
[11:25] Evan Ortiz: note for compliance we can limit logging fields and mask PII before shipping. masking is configured as a pipeline rule.
[11:36] Roberto Diaz: is there a mechanism to prevent accidental model version drift between staging and prod? we need checks in CI.
[11:44] Jordan Mills: we recommend pinning model versions and using the Console's rollout API in your CI to ensure deployments are explicit. we'll include a CI example in the repo.
[11:55] Priya Shah: couple more caveats — if you choose peering, we need to avoid overlapping CIDRs; if you choose endpoint service in our account, you'll need to accept service principals and hold the interface endpoints in your account. also note that private endpoints are region-bound and AZ-aware.
[12:18] Maya Chen: what about IPv6? we plan to enable IPv6 later this year.
[12:25] Priya Shah: we're primarily IPv4 today, but we can discuss IPv6 options; current interface endpoint patterns are IPv4-first.
[12:33] Tom Adler: legal will want the data ingress/egress diagram exported for audit.
[12:39] Jordan Mills: we'll produce a network handoff doc with diagrams and a short runbook for your ops team.
[12:46] Maya Chen: can you give a ballpark for cost differences between hosted private endpoints on shared infra vs dedicated in-vpc GPU pools?
[12:55] Jordan Mills: rough rule of thumb: hosted-private (shared infra + private endpoints) is lower base cost but variable per-token compute; Dedicated in-vpc has a higher fixed monthly commitment but lower unit cost for high throughput or large batch jobs. we'll follow up with a more precise estimate tailored to your expected QPS/embedding batch size.
[13:18] Sana Qureshi: timeline for support SLA? we need a 24x7 pager for production inference.
[13:25] Evan Ortiz: enterprise tiers include 24x7 on-call with escalation; Dedicated customers get faster response SLOs. we'll share the SLA doc.
[13:33] Roberto Diaz: will you provide an architecture review template for our security team? they tend to ask the same 20 questions.
[13:40] Priya Shah: yes we'll provide the security questionnaire and a completed example for a finance customer.
[13:47] Jordan Mills: ok, i want to recap real quick — action items: priya will produce terraform + diagram, jordan will send SOC2/KMS docs, maya will share cidrs and transit-gw inventory, and we'll schedule the pilot kickoff.
[13:59] Tom Adler: one last ask — we need to vet third-party dependencies for any open source bits in your runtime. do you publish SBOM?
[14:07] Evan Ortiz: yes we can provide a Software Bill of Materials and an image list for the runtime components.
[14:15] Maya Chen: thanks all, this was helpful.
[14:18] Jordan Mills: thank you, we'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with the initial docs and a proposed pilot calendar.
[14:26] [00:52:00] -- meeting end --
